content: Pseudodysphagia, also known as the fear of choking, is characterized by an irrational fear of swallowing or choking. The symptoms associated with this condition are psychosomatic in nature. Individuals with pseudodysphagia mentally associate the act of swallowing with choking or with an imagined inability of the esophageal opening to function properly. This mental association can trigger panic reactions either before or during the act of swallowing. The sensation of difficulty in swallowing feels very real to the affected individual, even though it is not based on any actual physical abnormality. It is crucial to rule out dysphagia, which refers to genuine difficulty or pain during swallowing, before diagnosing pseudodysphagia. The fear of choking is often linked to underlying psychological conditions such as anxiety, depression, panic attacks, hypochondriasis, and even weight loss. This condition can manifest in both children and adults and occurs equally in males and females. It can have a profound impact on the individual’s quality of life. People with pseudodysphagia may avoid restaurants or social settings due to their fear, as they often feel the need to consume food in very small bites or only with liquids to mitigate their anxiety.
